original_title: Enantioconvergent Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling for the Synthesis of α-Aryl Ketones via Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
title: Two different carboxylic acids, one chiral ketone
blurb: Photoredox/nickel catalysis couples α-aryl carboxylic acid derivatives with aliphatic carboxylic acids in an enantioconvergent decarboxylative coupling, landing on enantioenriched α-aryl ketones while keeping the usual decarboxylative side reactions, protodecarboxylation and homocoupling, from taking over. The trick is getting two structurally different acid partners to react with each other instead of with themselves.

original_title: Synergistic RhFe Single-Atom Alloy and Nanoalloy Sites for Highly Efficient and Robust Heterogeneous Hydroformylation
title: Splitting rhodium's two jobs onto two different sites fixes heterogeneous hydroformylation
blurb: Heterogeneous hydroformylation has a built-in conflict: whatever makes a catalyst tolerate CO also tends to choke off H2 activation, on top of Rh just leaching away regardless. The fix is a dual-site RhFe catalyst on hydroxyapatite, single-atom alloy sites and nanoalloy sites doing separate jobs, which gets over 99% conversion and selectivity on styrenic and C6-C10 olefins at a mild 60°C, plus a turnover frequency above 30,000/h for propene at 110°C. Numbers like that out of a heterogeneous Rh system are the real news here.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Photochemical Hetero-cycloadditions
title: A survey of what light can do to cycloadditions that heat can't
blurb: A review rounding up two decades of photochemical and photocatalytic hetero-cycloadditions, the heterocycle-building reactions that only work because an excited state opens radical, ionic, or excited-state pathways thermal chemistry never reaches. Useful as a map of the field rather than a new result.

original_title: Characterization and Nanoparticle Immobilization of a Thermotogaceae Esterase Active on Aromatic and Aliphatic Esters
title: A thermophile esterase that doesn't care if your ester is aromatic or aliphatic
blurb: TbEst, pulled out of a Thermotogaceae thermophile, is a classic α/β-hydrolase with the usual Ser-His-Asp triad, cloned, expressed, purified, and then immobilized on nanoparticles. It hydrolyzes both aromatic and aliphatic esters, the kind of broad tolerance that's actually useful at industrial scale rather than a one-trick enzyme.

original_title: Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
title: Triplet nitrenes trigger a formal semipinacol route to quaternary carbons
blurb: Visible light generates triplet nitrene species in situ that kick off a formal semipinacol rearrangement of tertiary allyl alcohols, redox-neutral, building both cyclic and linear all-carbon quaternary centers through an alkyl-migration pathway that's barely been explored next to the usual ring-contraction versions. Quaternary carbons are a pain to assemble in general, which is what makes a modular photochemical route to them stand out.

original_title: LiH/FePcG-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis via Interfacial Hydride-Mediated Dinitrogen Activation
title: A lithium hydride assist gets ammonia synthesis going under mild conditions
blurb: LiH paired with an Fe-N-C catalyst (FePcG) couples at the interface so the hydride helps activate N2 directly instead of leaving the Fe sites to crack the N≡N bond alone. Isotopic labeling, in situ DRIFTS, and gas-phase mass spec back up the mechanism rather than just asserting it. Still catalyst chemistry, not a Haber-Bosch replacement, but mild-condition N2 activation is the part everyone's actually chasing.

original_title: NMR Spectroscopic Evidence for Magnetically Induced Ring Currents in All-Metal-Aromatic [Bi4]4+
title: Proving a bismuth ring is aromatic, not just DFT saying so
blurb: All-metal aromaticity claims usually lean on calculations, since heavy elements like bismuth muddy NMR signatures with local magnetic effects. Here they pin down actual magnetically induced ring currents in a [Bi4]4+ cluster using solid- and solution-state NMR, SQUID magnetometry, and relativistic calculations, leaning on an isostructural Li4Br-encapsulated analogue and a Bi(III) reference compound to strip the ring current signal out of the heavy-atom noise.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Single-Cell Mass Spectrometry with Enhanced Coverage of cis -Diol Metabolites via a Reactive Pulled Flowprobe in Static-Zone Enrichment Sampling Mode
title: Squeezing more metabolites out of a single cell
blurb: Single-cell MS usually misses low-abundance, poorly ionizable stuff like cis-diol metabolites. This pulled flowprobe parks a stationary sample band inside a flowing liquid microjunction, buying enough dwell time to enrich and derivatize those metabolites in place before they ever hit the detector.

original_title: Transient-Directing Group-Enabled Manganese-Catalyzed C–H Alkylation
title: Manganese C-H activation gets its first transient directing group
blurb: Mn-catalyzed C-H activation has been stuck installing permanent directing groups and then having to strip them back off. Here a catalytic, transient one drives intramolecular C-H alkylation on indole-3-carboxaldehydes instead, building N1/C2-fused polycyclic indoles with a new tertiary carbon center in excellent yield. One less synthetic step tax.

original_title: General Asymmetric Synthesis of Noncanonical Amino Acids
title: A general route to noncanonical amino acids, starting from plain carboxylic acids
blurb: Turns ordinary carboxylic acids into alpha-ketoesters, then runs a lipase hydrolysis-transamination cascade to deliver the noncanonical amino acid. The broad scope is the point, since most routes to these building blocks are one-off syntheses rather than something you can reuse across targets.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Engineering the Interfacial Microenvironment to Boost Ethane Dehydrogenation on Ga2O3-Pt Catalysts via Metal Doping Modulation
title: Doping Ga2O3-Pt so ethane dehydrogenation stops wasting hydrogen
blurb: Plain Ga2O3-Pt is tuned for propane and does ethane dehydrogenation badly, low ethylene-formation activity and only 84% selectivity, because its interfacial sites bind hydrogen too uniformly to discriminate between pathways. DFT plus kinetic Monte Carlo here test single-atom-doped variants to see if tuning that interfacial hydrogen adsorption fixes it. All computational so far, a prediction waiting on someone to actually run it.

original_title: Indium-Catalyzed Deaminative Coupling of Propargylamines with Terminal Alkynes: A Mild Approach to Conjugated 1,3-Dienones
title: Indium turns propargylamines and alkynes into dienones with no fuss
blurb: InCl3 and DBU hydrolyze propargylamines to enones in situ, then couple them with terminal alkynes via syn-selective alkyne insertion to give conjugated 1,3-dienones in good to excellent yield. Mild conditions and broad functional-group tolerance, with indium doing a job that usually goes to a flashier metal.

original_title: A Substrate-Permissive Vanadium Haloperoxidase in Type II Polyketide Biosynthesis Unlocks Non-Native Halogenation across Diverse Substrate Scaffolds
title: A vanadium haloperoxidase that'll chlorinate almost anything you hand it
blurb: Most halogenases are picky about substrates, which is what keeps enzymatic halogenation from being more widely used. XhnO11, a secreted vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase from Streptomyces xinghaiensis, handles the chlorination step in making the anticancer agent xinghaicarcin A, and turns out to tolerate a wide range of substrate scaffolds beyond its native one. That permissiveness is the actual find here, not just another halogenase.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: DBU-Catalyzed One-Pot Domino Synthesis of Polycyclic Benzofuran(thiophene)-pyridine-Fused Indolizines
title: One DBU pot, four bonds, and a fused indolizine falls out
blurb: A DBU-catalyzed domino reaction runs a Knoevenagel condensation straight into a [4+1] cycloaddition/cyclization cascade on a pyridinylacetonitrile, an aroyl-benzofuran or -benzothiophene carbaldehyde, and TMSCN, fusing five- and six-membered rings into polycyclic benzofuran/thiophene-pyridine-indolizines under mild conditions. Four bond-forming events without touching the flask in between.

original_title: Copper-Photocatalyzed 1,2-Boron Migrative Alkylation of β-Boryl NHPI Esters with Cyclopropanols
title: Boron takes a walk before the alkylation even starts
blurb: Photoredox and copper catalysis combine to shift a boron group over by one carbon on beta-boryl NHPI esters, generating a radical that copper then intercepts with an alkyl group pulled from ring-opening a cyclopropanol. The bulky terpyridine ligand is apparently doing real mechanistic work here, not just sitting on the metal for show.

original_title: Proton-Donor Identity Shapes Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction on Silver
title: Sorting out what's actually happening in silver's messy nitrate reduction voltammograms
blurb: Nitrate reduction on silver gives cyclic voltammograms with multiple cathodic features that nobody fully agrees on the mechanism for. Pairing CV with SECM for in situ product detection and RDE hydrodynamics, they show proton donor identity reshapes which pathway actually dominates. A mechanistic cleanup more than a new catalyst.

original_title: Synthesis and Reactivity of Substituted Phosphanylalanes and ‐Gallanes Stabilized by N‐Heterocyclic Carbenes
title: NHC carbenes babysitting unstable phosphorus-gallium and phosphorus-aluminum hydrides
blurb: Salt metathesis between IDipp-coordinated gallium and aluminum halides and alkali metal phosphanides gives a set of NHC-stabilized phosphanylgallanes and phosphanylalanes. The aluminum versions are described as highly temperature sensitive, but the gallium ones held still long enough for X-ray structures: monomeric, distorted tetrahedral at the metal. Mostly a stabilization trick, but a useful one for a class of compounds that usually doesn't sit around long enough to characterize.

original_title: Switching ATP‐Forming Phosphoryl‐Transfer Chemistry With a Restricted Set of Amino Acids
title: An enzyme missing its catalytic histidine still makes ATP
blurb: They rebuilt an ancestral nucleoside diphosphate kinase using only 10 prebiotically plausible amino acids plus lysine and arginine, no histidine allowed even though that's the residue textbooks say does the catalysis. The variant keeps the NDK fold and still disproportionates ADP into ATP and AMP, an activity the authors say wasn't detectable before. So cutting the amino acid alphabet down doesn't just cripple the enzyme, it seems to reroute the chemistry entirely.

original_title: Enantioselective Benzylic C–H Insertions with Diazosuccinate Esters
title: Diazosuccinate esters finally get their C-H insertion
blurb: First enantioselective benzylic C-H insertion run on α-alkyl-α-diazoesters, using a standard chiral dirhodium catalyst, hitting up to 95% ee on primary benzylic C-H bonds. The payoff is the diester product: one ester comes off selectively, leaving a free carboxylic acid for further elaboration. A reagent class that's been sitting around underused finally has a reason to get used.

original_title: Fischer Indole Synthesis Inspired De Novo and Modular Assembly of Indolines
title: Indolines built straight from plain anilines, no oxidation or reduction needed
blurb: Instead of prefunctionalized arenes or redox steps, this one-pot sequence starts from ortho-unsubstituted anilines and vinyldiazoacetates: rhodium-catalyzed N-H insertion, then a TFA-promoted aza-Claisen rearrangement, then an intramolecular aza-Michael to close the ring. Redox-neutral and broad in substrate scope, which is the part that makes a modular de novo route actually worth adopting.

original_title: Asymmetric Dipolar Cycloadditions toward Chiral Medium-Sized Rings under Palladium and Iridium Catalysis
title: Making 7- to 11-membered rings chiral is still mostly a Pd/Ir problem
blurb: A rundown of why medium rings are the annoying middle child of ring synthesis, too flexible for easy stereocontrol and too big for the usual small-ring tricks, and how palladium- and iridium-catalyzed asymmetric dipolar cycloadditions have become the go-to strategy for getting chirality into them anyway. Reads like a field summary rather than a single new result, useful if you need the state of the art in one place.

original_title: Access to Axially Chiral Biaryl Aldehydes via Enantioselective Imine Condensation
title: Chiral phosphoric acid turns imine condensation into an atropisomer sorter
blurb: Axially chiral biaryl aldehydes made by chiral-phosphoric-acid-catalyzed imine condensation, either desymmetrizing a prochiral substrate or kinetically resolving a racemic atropisomer mixture. The aldehydes aren't the end product, they're feedstock for further asymmetric catalysis and materials work, which is really the point of making them this way.

original_title: FDA Approves Curium’s Lutathera Generic Bexlutry After Novartis Patent Scuffle - Genome Web
title: Lutathera gets its first generic, after a patent fight with Novartis
blurb: FDA approved Curium's Bexlutry as a generic version of Novartis's Lutathera, the lutetium-177 therapy for neuroendocrine tumors, following a patent dispute between the two companies. Whatever that dispute turned on, the upshot is a second supplier for a radiopharmaceutical that's historically had exactly one.

original_title: Pd-catalyzed Cycloadditions of 5-Vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones: A Diastereo- and Enantioselective Access to Spirooxindoles
title: Spirooxindoles from a cycloaddition partner nobody's used for this before
blurb: Pd-catalyzed cycloaddition of 5-vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones with isatins builds spirooxindoles, with DTBM-SEGPHOS doing the work of setting two new tetrasubstituted stereocenters with high diastereo- and enantiocontrol. The authors note broad functional group tolerance, and flag this as a rare case of this cycloaddition partner reacting with an electrophilic C=O at all, so the scope claim is doing real work here, not just padding.

original_title: Synthesis of Chiral α-Aminophosphonate Derivatives through Copper(I)-Catalyzed Enantioselective Alkylation
title: Copper lets you build chiral α-aminophosphonates by alkylation instead of the usual routes
blurb: A Cu(I)-catalyzed enantioselective alkylation of N-protected aminomethylthiophosphonates, using allyl, propargyl, benzyl bromides and alkyl iodides as the electrophiles, gives chiral α-aminophosphonate derivatives through actual C-C bond formation, which the authors note is the part existing methods are bad at. Control experiments back up the mechanism they propose.

original_title: Highly Carboxylated Cellulose Microspheres via Alginate Pre-Grafting for High-Resolution and High-Capacity Weak Cation Exchange Chromatography
title: Cellulose microspheres get grafted with alginate before they get carboxylated
blurb: Their earlier crosslinked cellulose microspheres already worked as a weak cation-exchange matrix, but grafting alginate onto them first before deep carboxylation pushes the carboxyl density up, aiming at the usual WCX tradeoff of needing both high binding capacity and high resolution at once. A packing-material fix, not flashy, but protein purification runs on exactly this kind of incremental improvement.

original_title: Atomic Site-Specific Eigenstrain for Efficient Electrocatalysis
title: Mapping strain atom by atom in Pt catalysts
blurb: Most strain-engineering work only tracks the average surface strain, but this maps eigenstrain, the local anisotropic strain, site by site across Pt nanoclusters. Activity against eigenstrain traces a volcano curve rather than a straight line, so the sites that help aren't the most strained ones, they're the ones strained just right.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Macrocyclization of ω‐Isocyano Aldehydes
title: Passerini and Ugi reactions talked into closing macrocycles
blurb: Macrocycles are a pain to close because the ring-closing step fights you kinetically and thermodynamically. Here omega-isocyano aldehydes run through Passerini and Ugi multicomponent reactions to build medium rings and macrocyclic alpha-amino amides/acids directly, skipping the usual stepwise route.

original_title: Composition-Dependent Remodeling of the ABCB1Disordered Linker by Plasma-Generated ReactiveMixtures
title: Cold plasma attacks P-glycoprotein where the drugs can't
blurb: Active-site inhibitors of ABCB1, the pump that exports chemo drugs out of cancer cells, keep failing clinically from off-target toxicity, so this goes after the disordered linker between its two halves instead. Cold atmospheric plasma's mix of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species remodels that linker differently depending on the mixture's composition, a mechanical-coupling attack rather than a blocking one.

original_title: Design, Synthesis, and Pharmacological Profiling of Serine/Threonine Kinase 33 (STK33) Inhibitors for Nonhormonal Male Contraception
title: A non-hormonal male contraceptive candidate gets its solubility fixed
blurb: STK33 is both genetically and chemically validated as a male germ-specific contraceptive target, but their earlier compound CDD-2807 had poor kinetic solubility. SAR and SPR work on the same indazole scaffold produced CDD-3094, which keeps nanomolar cellular potency while fixing that liability.

original_title: Controlled Hydrogen Delivery by Single‐Atom Ru Accelerates Electrocatalytic Ammonia Synthesis
title: Single Ru atoms play water-splitter for ammonia electrocatalysis
blurb: NO-to-ammonia electroreduction usually loses efficiency to competing pathways, so isolated Ru atoms on Co3O4 are installed to do one job, split water and hand off surface-bound H, forcing the reaction down a Langmuir-Hinshelwood route. A dedicated hydrogen-delivery step bolted onto the catalyst rather than a broadly better one.

original_title: A soluble conductive chromium coordination polymer with radical ligands and non-integer redox states
title: A chromium polymer that conducts in solution and counts electrons in fractions
blurb: Linking CrIII ions to electron-poor bis-terpyridine ligands gives something rare, a conductive coordination polymer you can actually process in solution, with the Cr driving the ligands into radical and dianion states. In DMF it shifts charge in non-integer steps, which is the kind of electronic behavior you don't usually get from a MOF analog.

original_title: Cu(I)-Photosensitizer Catalysis: A Tool for Conjunctive Olefination of Aldehydes
title: A Wittig workaround that skips building the phosphonium salt from scratch
blurb: Standard Wittig chemistry needs alkyl halides to make its phosphonium salts, which locks out a lot of complex substrates. Cu(I)-photosensitizer catalysis instead takes one commercial vinyl phosphonium salt and extends it under visible light into a range of Wittig precursors, sidestepping the alkyl halide step entirely.

original_title: Crystal Phase-Dependent Electronic Metal-Support Interactions Enable Chemoselective Hydrogenation of α, β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
title: Which Nb2O5 crystal phase you pick decides what the Ir clusters hydrogenate
blurb: Same Ir nanoclusters, different polymorphs of the Nb2O5 support underneath, and the electronic metal-support interaction shifts enough to change selectivity on alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehydes. The orthorhombic Nb2O5-T phase forms a distinct socketed contact with the metal that the spectroscopy actually resolves, so this reads as a real support-engineering lever rather than a footnote.

original_title: Breaking symmetry for better catalysis
title: Lopsided sulfide catalysts handle the arenes symmetric ones won't
blurb: Sulfide catalysts are fine at aromatic halogenation until the arene gets less reactive, where they usually stall out. Breaking the catalyst's own symmetry opens up sulfur orbital interactions that weren't accessible before, stretching the scope to those harder substrates.

original_title: Chiral Cycloparaarylenes Incorporating Binaphthyl Units: Dramatic Effects of Peripheral Functionalization on (Chir)Optical Properties
title: Swap methoxy for a methylenedioxy bridge and a chiral nanohoop changes its whole shape
blurb: Two chiral [12]cycloparaarylenes built from binaphthyl and biphenyl units differ only in one peripheral group, methoxy versus a methylenedioxy bridge, but that's enough to lock one into a fixed D3-symmetric transoid structure while the other equilibrates between C3 and C1 cisoid forms. A small peripheral change reaching all the way into the macrocycle's symmetry and its optical behavior.

original_title: Synthesis of Pyrroloquinazolinones via Base-Promoted Domino Reaction of 7-Vinylindoles with In Situ Formed Isocyanates from Dioxazolones
title: Indoles plus dioxazolones, no metal required
blurb: 7-Vinylindoles meet isocyanates generated on the fly from dioxazolones, and a base talks them through decarboxylation, a Lossen rearrangement, then two additions in one pot to build pyrroloquinazolinones. No transition metal anywhere, yields up to 95%, and you get a fused polycyclic indole scaffold for the price of mixing two simple reagents.

original_title: Single-molecule reaction chambers reveal intramolecular protein kinase activation
title: Kinases phosphorylating themselves, caught in the act
blurb: The textbook story has one kinase domain phosphorylating another's activation loop in trans, but bulk assays can't actually tell intra- from intermolecular since the chemistry looks identical either way. Single-molecule reaction chambers can tell, and they find activation happening within a single kinase, not between two. That's a real mechanistic distinction, not a technicality, since it changes what a cell needs for a fast, graded response.

original_title: Mechanistic Basis of Sulfo Transfer in a PAPS-Independent ArylSulfate SulfoTransferases Revealed by Crystallography and QM/MM Simulations
title: Sulfation without the expensive cofactor, mechanism included
blurb: Arylsulfate sulfotransferases skip PAPS entirely and just use cheap aryl sulfate donors like pNPS, which is why they're appealing biocatalysts for green sulfation chemistry. Crystallography plus QM/MM now lays out how the enzyme positions donor and acceptor and forms the covalent sulfo-enzyme intermediate, which is the part you need nailed down before anyone can engineer these things on purpose.

original_title: Enhanced Electrochemical C–N Coupling for Glycine Synthesis via an Active Hydrogen Pump
title: Glycine made by electrochemistry, not fermentation
blurb: An indium-doped bismuth catalyst co-reduces oxalic acid and nitrate straight into glycine, hitting 83.3% Faradaic efficiency at an honestly industrial 361 mA/cm² and 4.3 mol/h per gram of catalyst, beating plain bismuth. Still a lab cell, but that current density is the number that would actually matter for scaling this past a proof of concept.

original_title: Unanticipated intermediates during isopenicillin N synthase catalysis identified by time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser studies
title: Watching isopenicillin N synthase mid-reaction
blurb: Time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser snapshots catch transient states in isopenicillin N synthase as it activates oxygen and closes the beta-lactam ring, intermediates that static structures never held still long enough to show. Protein dynamics and the solvent network turn out to be doing real work in steering the chemistry, not just sitting there as scaffold.

original_title: Energetics of Proton‐Coupled Electron Transfer in Hydroxy‐Bridged Dicopper Complexes with N ‐Heterocyclic Carbene (NHC) Ligands
title: Mapping how hard a dicopper core works to pull an O–H bond apart
blurb: A set of NHC-ligated, hydroxo-bridged dicopper(II) complexes stands in for the copper-oxygen core of particulate methane monooxygenase, and tuning redox potentials and pKa's across the series maps out O–H bond dissociation free energies spanning 68.5 to 106.7 kcal/mol. Swapping ligands barely moves some of the underlying parameters, which is the kind of decoupling that's more informative than if everything had moved together.

original_title: Closed-Loop CO2-Mediated Ultrafast and Controlled Synthesis of Amino Acid Polymers toward a Circular Carbon and Polymer Economy
title: Amino acid polymers that start and end as CO2
blurb: A CO2-mediated route builds amino acid polyamides fast and with real control over molecular weight, dodging the slow, poorly controlled polymerizations that usually plague this class and that usually bleed CO2 in the process instead of using it as feedstock. The pitch is a closed loop where the carbon and the polymer both get reused, which is the part worth watching once someone runs the actual recycling numbers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Active-site nanoconfinement for prolonged radical reactivity
title: Squeezing a radical's lifetime by boxing it in
blurb: Confining an active site keeps a radical reactive for longer than it would stick around in free solution. That's the whole claim on offer here, with no scope or mechanism detail to chew on yet.

original_title: Photobiocatalytic Diastereo- and Enantioselective Synthesis of Non-Canonical Amino Acids Bearing Challenging Stereochemical Dyads and Triads
title: Evolving an enzyme to pick its own stereochemistry, dyad or triad
blurb: Starting from a thermophilic tryptophan synthase beta-subunit, directed evolution produces PLP-dependent biocatalysts that branch into complementary families, one making non-canonical amino acids with skipped gamma-stereocenters, another with contiguous beta,gamma triads. Getting a radical C-C coupling to hit multiple stereocenters on demand, and controllably, is the part that's usually been out of reach for this kind of acyclic target.

original_title: Cooperative Fe–LMCT and Ni–S H 2 Catalysis for Native Carboxylic Acid Methyl Editing
title: Turning a carboxylic acid straight into a methyl group
blurb: Fe-mediated LMCT photocatalysis strips a free carboxylic acid down to an alkyl radical, and Ni-mediated SH2 radical sorting then wires it into a new sp3–sp3 C–C bond, together editing a native carboxylic acid into a methyl group without ever touching a C–H bond. A genuine alternative route to methylation that starts from a functional group everything already has lying around.

original_title: S = 3/2 Iron(I)‐Bisphosphine‐Ate Complexes: Synthesis, Characterization, and Reactivity for Electrophile Activation
title: What Fe(I) actually looks like before it grabs a C–X bond
blurb: Low-coordinate Fe(I)-bisphosphine species get invoked constantly as the active species behind C-Cl/Br/I activation, but nobody's actually pinned down their electronic structure. This isolates and characterizes an S = 3/2 Fe(I)-ate complex and tests its electrophile activation directly, putting a real structure behind what's usually just a postulated intermediate.

original_title: Depth-resolved operando grazing-incidence diffraction reveals non-equilibrium Cu-Pt alloy restructuring under glycerol electrooxidation
title: Watching a Cu-Pt catalyst rearrange itself while it works
blurb: Cu-Pt alloys get more active toward glycerol electrooxidation once you electrochemically activate them, but that activation scrambles the structure in poorly understood ways. Depth-resolved operando grazing-incidence diffraction follows the restructuring in real time under actual alkaline reaction conditions, not just before-and-after snapshots.

original_title: Mechanistic Study of a Thermal- and Light-Driven Single-Crystal-to-Single-Crystal Transformation of an Organocerium Complex
title: A crystal that isomerizes itself and lets you watch
blurb: A CeIV-cyclopropenyl complex rearranges into its allenyl isomer via heat or light, and because it does it single-crystal-to-single-crystal, the structure survives intact enough to catch the mechanism mid-transformation instead of just inferring it from the starting and ending points.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Trifunctional antibody fusion proteins for targeted co-delivery of 4-1BBL with IL-15 or IL-21 to enhance antitumor immune responses
title: Stapling two immune signals onto one antibody instead of dosing them separately
blurb: Single-payload antibody fusions aren't cutting it against tumors on their own, so this builds a trifunctional fusion protein: a tumor-targeting Fab fused to the costimulatory ligand 4-1BBL plus either IL-15 or IL-21. The bet is that delivering both signals together, locally, beats giving either cytokine alone.

original_title: Synthesis of USP Grade [2,3,7‐ 13 C 3 ]‐Nicotinamide for Human Pharmacokinetic Studies
title: Making a 13C-tagged vitamin pure enough to actually give to people
blurb: Five synthetic steps, 17.8 g, 42% overall yield, and USP-grade purity gets you [2,3,7-13C3]-nicotinamide ready for human PK studies. The three labeled carbons sit where metabolism can't easily strip them, and it turns out three heavy atoms are enough for better than 1000:1 mass spec resolution against the unlabeled stuff.
venue: Journal of Labelled Compounds and Radiopharmaceuticals

original_title: Persistent Mn 3+ Sites on Reduced MnO Enable Efficient Syngas Conversion
title: MnO's real active site is the Mn3+ impurity everyone overlooked
blurb: Everyone treats MnO as the active phase for syngas conversion, but catalysts that converge on the same bulk MnO structure still perform differently depending on their starting oxide. Time-resolved X-ray absorption plus depth-resolved synchrotron analysis traces the real driver to trace Mn3+ sites stranded on oxygen-deficient surfaces, not the bulk phase at all.

original_title: Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering Covalency Analysis Reveals Non-Aufbau Electronic Configurations in Low-Valent Lanthanides
title: Divalent lanthanides breaking the Aufbau principle, now with a number attached
blurb: Some divalent lanthanide ions settle into 4f^n5d^1 configurations that formally shouldn't happen under normal orbital filling. RIXS and HERFD-XANES on a series of [M(NHAriPr6)2] complexes quantify how much 5d character actually mixes into the bonding, turning a qualitative oddity into an actual covalency measurement.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: High-Entropy Lanthanoid Oxide Catalysts for Oxidative Coupling of Methane
title: Five lanthanides, one oxide, better methane coupling
blurb: High-entropy oxides usually get sold on robustness, not the precise selectivity oxidative coupling of methane actually demands. A (LaSmEuGdDy)0.4O3 catalyst made by sol-gel with aspartic acid is pitched as getting both: tunable surface basicity without giving up structural stability at low OCM temperatures.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Integrating a Tumor Size-Overall Survival Model Into a Spatial Quantitative Systems Pharmacology Framework for Antibody-Drug Conjugates in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
title: Linking tumor shrinkage to survival in one pharmacology model
blurb: A tumor size-overall survival model gets folded into a spatial quantitative systems pharmacology framework for antibody-drug conjugates in non-small-cell lung cancer, aiming to connect how much a tumor shrinks directly to a survival prediction instead of treating the two as separate endpoints.

original_title: Structure–Activity Relationships in Methyl‐Driven Overhauser Effect DNP
title: Making Overhauser DNP actually work at high field
blurb: Cross-effect DNP leans on nitroxide biradicals that clash with plenty of samples and lose efficiency as field strength climbs. Overhauser-effect DNP could dodge both problems with a broader menu of radicals, and this works out the structure-activity relationships for methyl-functionalized, mixed-valence conjugated radicals as the polarizing agents.

original_title: Terminal Oxygen as a Proton Acceptor: S–H Activation via Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer in Decavanadate-Catalyzed P(O)–S Coupling
title: A vanadium cluster that babysits the proton mid-transfer
blurb: Mechanistic dig into decavanadate-catalyzed coupling of phosphine oxide and thiophenol to make thiophosphates for drugs and pesticides. Turns out the slow step is S-H bond breaking via proton-coupled electron transfer, with a terminal oxygen on the cluster acting as a relay that stabilizes the proton in transit. Nice mechanistic clarity, still a coupling reaction looking for a bigger substrate scope.

original_title: Engineering Immune Cell Engagers: From Molecular Constructs to Biomaterial Platforms
title: Immune cell engagers move off the molecule and onto a scaffold
blurb: A review tracking immune cell engagers, the molecules that physically bridge immune cells to tumor cells to trigger killing or phagocytosis, as the field expands from standalone molecular constructs to biomaterial platforms. Framed as filling a gap checkpoint blockade leaves open: it can wake immune cells up but doesn't force the physical contact. It's a review, so no new data, just the state of play.

original_title: Topological Engineering of NIR‐II Emissive Conjugated Oligomers With Unexpected Excited‐State Manifolds for Efficient Phototheranostics and Cancer Immunotherapy
title: Bending a dye's topology to get imaging and therapy out of the same photon
blurb: NIR-II conjugated oligomers where changing the molecular topology reshuffles the excited-state pathways enough to boost fluorescence and phototherapeutic output together, instead of trading one for the other like usual. Pitched toward cancer phototheranostics and immunotherapy. Still a materials design result, not a treated animal.

original_title: Mapping the Energy Landscape of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon π–π Stacking Using a High‐Precision Torsional Balance Based on the 13,14‐Diphenyl‐6,7‐dihydrodibenzo[b,j][4,7]Phenanthroline Scaffold
title: A molecular balance built to actually weigh pi-stacking
blurb: A new torsional balance on a DHDBPT scaffold that's rigid enough to restrict rotation but flexible enough to sample different stacking geometries, so pi-pi stacking between PAHs can be measured rather than inferred from theory. Fluorine substitution gets used as the probe for how substituents shift the interaction.

original_title: Design and Synthesis of an Indoloquinoxaline Non‐Fullerene Acceptor—Polythiophene Donor‐Based Double Cable Polymer as an All‐Organic Photocatalyst for Artificial Photosynthesis of H 2 O 2
title: Welding the donor and acceptor into one backbone to split excitons faster
blurb: A double-cable polymer that covalently bonds a polythiophene donor to an indoloquinoxaline non-fullerene acceptor, so charge separation happens right on the backbone instead of relying on a blended-in acceptor that can phase-separate over time. The payoff is an all-organic photocatalyst that makes H2O2 from light, no metal needed.

original_title: Pd-Cu-Ag Trimetallic Synergistic Catalysis for Decarboxylative/Deaminative Coupling of Carboxylic acids with Tertiary Amines
title: Three metals team up to skip the usual ammonium salt detour
blurb: A Pd-Cu-Ag trimetallic system builds diphenylmethanes by cleaving C(sp3)-N bonds in tertiary amines and decarboxylating carboxylic acids at the same time, generating carbene intermediates in situ rather than going through the standard Suzuki or Hiyama coupling of benzylic ammonium salts. The decarboxylative route to this scaffold has barely been explored, so just getting it to work is the actual news.

original_title: What do you think of the book "The Chemists' Cookbook" by Lluís Llorens?
title: What do you think of the book "The Chemists' Cookbook" by Lluís Llorens?
blurb: Good afternoon. I work in medicinal chemistry, but my main focus is small-scale (milligram) organic synthesis. I’m looking for a more up-to-date book on synthetic methods (amidations, reductions, SNAr, etc.), something that covers, for instance, various ways to reduce a benzonitrile. Has anyone here bought The Chemists' Cookbook? Or is there a better option for my needs? I'm open to suggestions.

original_title: Isopropanol Peroxides found
title: Isopropanol Peroxides found
blurb: Chem professor here. One of our lab managers came across a bottle of crystallized isopropanol, and never having seen it before, I snapped a picture. Most of the pictures out there are clumps, whereas this had longer spikes. I hadn't seen it before in my 20+ years of chem, my army hazmat friend hadn't seen it, so I figured you r/chemistry folks would like to see it too. Hazmat came and picked it up and made a big hullaballoo (sp?) about it last night.
